question: In which group helium is included.?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Noble gas group.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Noble gas group **is a group of elements in the periodic table that includes **helium (He), neon (Ne), argon (Ar), krypton (Kr), xenon (Xe), and radon (Rn).** 
 
• These elements are characterized by having a **full outermost shell of electrons**, making them very **stable and unreactive. **** **
 
• This stability is due to the fact that they have achieved a **state of equilibrium** by filling their **outermost shells with electrons.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pnictogen group** is a group of elements in the periodic table that includes **nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), arsenic (As), antimony (Sb), bismuth (Bi), and moscovium (Mc).**

 
 
• These elements are characterized by having **five valence electrons** in their outermost shell.
 
 
 
• **Chalcogen group** is a group of elements in the periodic table that includes **oxygen (O), sulfur (S), selenium (Se), tellurium (Te), and polonium (Po).**
 
 
• These elements are characterized by having **six valence electron**s in their outermost shell.
 
 
 
• **Halogen group** is a group of elements in the periodic table that includes **fluorine (F), chlorine (Cl), bromine (Br), iodine (I), and astatine (At).**
 
 
• **​**These elements are characterized by having **seven valence electrons** in their outermost shell.
